title: Card Services Standard — Issue and Activation of Marlowe & Finch Gift Cards
content:
Every Marlowe & Finch Gift Cards card number is created inactive and becomes usable when it is activated. This standard governs how each kind is sold or issued, loaded, activated and dated.

## 1. Sale of purchasable cards

1.1 A purchasable card is sold for a value between the kind's smallest issue or load and its largest value of one card, with the kind's purchase fee.
1.2 Buying a card earns no Finch Circle points, and a card cannot be paid with Finch Notes.
1.3 A card purchase at or above the kind's fraud review trigger in one transaction is held for review before activation.
1.4 A corporate order needs at least the minimum number of cards per corporate order, and receives the corporate volume discount at or above the corporate order value threshold for that discount.

## 2. Activation

2.1 A plastic card activates at the register.
2.2 A Marlowe & Finch eGift Card activates when it is delivered by one of the kind's digital delivery channels, on a date up to the kind's furthest scheduled delivery days ahead.
2.3 Online redemption of a card opens once the kind's online fraud hold, counted in hours from activation, has passed.

## 3. Store-issued cards and Bonus Cards

3.1 Store-issued cards (the Merchandise Credit Card and the Registry Reward Card) and Marlowe & Finch Bonus Cards are created in the customer's name, as the kind's issued-in-the-name-of term states.
3.2 Each such card is loaded once, by a single issue for the exact amount the issuing rule settles, and is activated on issue.
3.3 A return refund placed on a card always uses a new Merchandise Credit Card.
3.4 A Merchandise Credit Card issued for a no-receipt return records the returning customer's identification where the kind's identification-record term is yes.
3.5 A return of a purchase paid with a card is refunded onto a new card only where the paying kind's refund-onto-a-card term is yes.

## 4. Expiry date

4.1 A card is given an expiry date only when its kind's value expires.
4.2 The expiry date is the issue date plus the kind's validity period in days, less one day.

## 5. Form, number, resend and balance inquiry

5.1 Each kind comes in its own form (plastic or digital) and comes into existence in the way its kind states (purchase, store issue, corporate order or promotion), with a card number in the kind's card number format.
5.2 An eGift email that did not arrive can be resent to a corrected address where the kind permits a resend.
5.3 Balances can be checked through the kind's balance inquiry channels.

## Issue reasons and the opening value

| How the card is obtained | Opening value |
|---|---|
| Sold at a register or online | The purchase amount, within the kind's load range |
| Corporate order | The purchase amount of each card |
| Store issue for a return refund | The exact amount the return settles, on a new Merchandise Credit Card |
| Store issue for registry rewards or a registry credit conversion | The exact amount the registry payout or conversion settles |
| Store issue for an alteration damage settlement | The exact amount the settlement settles |
| Promotion | The promotional bonus earned |

## Worked expiry date (hypothetical dates)

- A hypothetical Marlowe & Finch Bonus Card issued on 1 March, its kind's validity period being 45 days: 1 March plus 45 days is 15 April; less one day, the expiry date is 14 April.
- A hypothetical Merchandise Credit Card issued on any date receives no expiry date, because its kind's value does not expire.
